newsitem.title: MONACO: RALLYING-SAINZ BUILDS NARROW LEAD OVER WORLD CHAMPION MAKINEN.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SAINZ BUILDS NARROW LEAD OVER WORLD CHAMPION MAKINEN.

text.p: World champion Tommi Makinen of Finland and his rival Carlos Sainz were involved in a duel on slippery roads in the Monte Carlo rally on Monday with the Spanish driver leading by a meagre four seconds after three timed stages.

Makinen and Sainz, who had to let Belgian Freddy Loix in his Toyota Celica steal Sunday's show by winning the first timed stage using a part of the Monaco Grand Prix circuit, took charge in Monday's first two sections in the Ardeche mountains.

Sainz was the first to shine, taking the 19.41-km stretch from Labatiere to Lalouvesc in his brand new Ford Escort. The only one to follow the pace set by the Spaniard was Makinen in his Mitsubishi Lancer.
An astute choice of tyres and aggressive driving allowed the Finn to fight back by clocking the fastest time in the next timed stage, over 25.74 kms around St Bonnet le Froid.

Briton Colin McRae, the 1995 world champion, was two seconds slower as he set the second fastest time in that section in his Mitsubishi Lancer. Sainz, twice a Monte Carlo winner, had to be content with the third time a further two seconds back.
With three stages remaining on the second day of the season-opening rally, Sainz was four seconds ahead of Makinen in the overall standings with McRae third 23 seconds behind the leader.
The conditions were particulary challenging with wet roads on the lower parts of the picturesque Ardeche hills and ice and snow patches higher up.
"The key-factor will be the choice of tyres," predicted Sainz, who won the winter classic in 1991 and 1995.
The rally ends on Wednesday in Monte Carlo.
